pin.title: Acute Limb Ischemia: An Update on Diagnosis and Management.

excerpt_terms: acute limb ischemia initial management urgent anticoagulation unfractionated heparin vascular emergency revascularization strategy Rutherford duration comorbidities

metadata.authority: Peer-reviewed narrative clinical review in Journal of Clinical Medicine, not a primary guideline, consensus or systematic review.

supporting_quotes.quote: Urgent anticoagulation with unfractionated heparin (UFH) prevents thrombus propagation and preserves microcirculation
Patients with clinical suspicion of ALI should be addressed to emergency centers which have a 24-h/365-day vascular team available for diagnosis and management.

The therapeutic strategy will depend on type of occlusion (thrombus or embolus), location, type of conduit (artery of graft), Rutherford class, duration of ischemia, co-morbidities and therapy-related risks and outcomes.
Different revascularization strategies can be applied, either endovascular or surgical (thrombectomy, bypass and arterial repair).

scope_limits: Use only for urgent UFH and emergency vascular-team access in clearly salvageable adult ALI; no exact UFH dose supplied by these initial-care paragraphs.

The urgent UFH passage does not expressly state contraindication exceptions. Current ACC/AHA corroboration confirms those exceptions, but restricted guideline text is not retained as author/reviewer evidence. A no-active-bleeding/no-HIT scenario avoids an unsupported contraindication-management branch.
Do not use this source to rank open surgery universally above endovascular techniques. Its own treatment section individualizes by Rutherford grade, cause, anatomy, time and risk.

Do not apply its open-revascularization sentence to categoryIII/nonviable limbs. It conflicts with current ACC/AHA guidance. Retained excerpt currently contains that sentence; source content audit must not treat every statement as current.

conflicting_text.quote: Patients with an immediately threatened or nonviable limb, bypass graft with suspected infection, or contraindication to thrombolysis should undergo open revascularization.
conflicting_text.finding: Includes nonviable limb in a blanket open-revascularization recommendation. Current2024 guideline recommends primary amputation for irreversibly damaged categoryIII and individualized urgent revascularization for salvageable limbs. This makes an unrestricted use of the review unsuitable.

current_primary_corroboration.paraphrase: The2024 ACC/AHA multisociety guideline calls for urgent expert assessment, therapeutic intravenous UFH on diagnosis unless contraindicated, selection of revascularization for salvageable limbs, and primary amputation for irreversible categoryIII.
current_primary_corroboration.use: Read-only audit corroboration. No restricted body passage copied into source JSON or proposed retained evidence.

recommendation: A narrow secondary_clinical_review exact pin can substantiate stable immediate UFH/emergency access if calendar-year recency is intentional and concurrent recent sources govern reperfusion choice. Do not certify it as a primary guideline or complete standalone ALI authority.
